text: A report1 of hepatotoxicity possibly associat- ed with the use of Copaltra, a herbal preparation marketed as an adjunct in the treatment of diabetes mellitus and containing cen- taury and Coutarea latiflora (copalchi) (Rubiaceae). A further 5 cases had been reported to the French pharmacovigilance net- work. 1. Wurtz A-S, et al. Possible hepatotoxicity from Copaltra, an herb- al medicine. Ann Pharmacother 2002; 36: 941–2. Cereus Cactus; Night-blooming Cereus. Profile Cereus, the flowers and stems of night-blooming cereus (Selen- icereus grandiflorus; Cactus grandiflorus) (Cactaceae), is thought to have cardiac stimulant actions and has been used in various cardiovascular disorders. It has also been used as an an- thelmintic and in the treatment of rheumatism. Homoeopathy. Cereus has been used in homoeopathic medi- cines under the following names: Cactus; Selenicereus grandi- florus; Cactus grandiflorus.
